q: why is the Fermi Paradox unsettling
why is the Fermi Paradox so unsettling
tell me about the Fermi Paradox
a: The Fermi Paradox is the apparent contradiction between the high probability of extraterrestrial intelligence existing and the lack of evidence for it. Named after physicist Enrico Fermi who famously asked Where is everybody? during a 1950 conversation about extraterrestrial life. The paradox arises from the following reasoning: our galaxy contains hundreds of billions of stars, many with potentially habitable planets, and the universe is billions of years old - so even if interstellar travel is very difficult, alien civilizations should have had plenty of time to colonize the galaxy. Yet we see no evidence of them. Proposed solutions include the Great Filter theory (some step from non-life to advanced civilization is extremely unlikely, either behind us or ahead of us), the Zoo Hypothesis (aliens deliberately avoid contact), the Dark Forest theory (civilizations hide to avoid destruction), and the possibility that advanced civilizations inevitably destroy themselves. The paradox remains one of the most compelling and unsettling questions in science because every proposed solution has troubling implications for humanity's future - either intelligent life is extremely rare (meaning we might be alone), or civilizations tend to self-destruct before achieving interstellar colonization (suggesting a grim fate awaits us too).
